newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends locked limit up on cold damage.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends locked limit up on cold damage.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter futures settled up their 25-cent limit on fears that bitter cold weekend temperatures in the U.S. Plains damaged emerging wheat plants, traders said.
It was an eerily quiet session in the KCBT wheat futures pit as traders just stood around -- their business hindered by the activation of daily upper trading limits.

"This is a major event," said Charlie Sernatinger, director of commodity operations at Man International. He estimated that 100 to 150 million bushels of wheat were wiped out when freezing temperatures swept as far south as Texas.
Trading did go on in the options pit, however, where KCBT July wheat options were trading with synthetic gains at seven to 14 cents above the July futures price of $4.50 a bushel.
Traders said the pool of unfilled futures orders swelled to approximately eight million bushels, with four or five million bushels pooled in the July contract alone.
Traders reported hearing estimates of total U.S. wheat losses ranging from 95 to 250 million bushels, but many cautioned that it will be days or even weeks before the full extent of damage is known.
All KCBT wheat futures out to March 1998 ended locked up their 25-cent limit, with July at $4.50 and May at $4.76.
